pageTitle: Lesson 24 · No Thanks and Thank You
eyebrow: Lesson 24 · B1 · Good Table Manners · 20 câu
heading: No Thanks and Thank You
source: Bài đọc phỏng theo Good Table Manners – Ann Ingalls (The Child's World, 2013), tr. 16–21.
credit: Tranh minh hoạ: Ronnie Rooney, trong Good Table Manners (The Child's World, 2013). Dùng cho mục đích học tập.

paras.label: A
paras.text: Not everyone likes the same food, so it's useful to know how to {refuse|refuse} politely. If a dish is new to you, try a tiny bite first; you might like it more than you expect. But if you really don't {fancy|fancy} fish eggs or frog's legs, simply say, "No, thank you." Never say, "That smells {rotten|rotten}!" You could hurt your host's feelings.

paras.label: B
paras.text: Remember that cooking dinner for guests takes a lot of {effort|effort}. Think about that before you say anything {unkind|unkind} about the food.

paras.label: C
paras.text: When the meal is over, say something nice to the cook and the host, and thank them for the delicious food. If you didn't enjoy it, you can still find something kind to say, like, "The flowers on the table are so pretty!"

paras.label: D
paras.text: Wait to be {excused|excused} before you leave the table. Until then, stay in your seat, listen to the conversation and {join in|join in} if you like. And, of course, thank your host for inviting you.

paras.label: E
paras.text: Now you know which fork to use and which way to pass the pasta. Keep practising, and soon you will {impress|impress} everyone with your table manners. You might even be invited back! Before long, your manners will be {finger-licking good|finger-licking good}.

parts.title: Part 1 · Which paragraph?
parts.instr: Đoạn nào (A–E) chứa thông tin dưới đây?

items.label: A paragraph that gives an example of a kind comment that isn't about the food
items.why: Đoạn C: khen hoa trên bàn.

items.label: A paragraph that suggests tasting something before deciding
items.why: Đoạn A: *try a tiny bite first.*

items.label: A paragraph that encourages you to keep practising
A paragraph that reminds you how hard cooking can be
items.why: Đoạn B: *takes a lot of effort.*

items.label: A paragraph that explains when you may leave the table

parts.title: Part 2 · Reading comprehension
parts.instr: Chọn đáp án đúng hoặc True / False.

questions.q: What does the writer suggest if a food is new to you?
Saying "That smells rotten!" is a polite way to refuse food.
questions.why: Sai. *Never say… You could hurt your host's feelings.*

questions.q: Why should you avoid saying unkind things about the food?
options: The host has made a big effort to cook it.
The other guests will eat it.
It may come from a restaurant.
questions.why: *cooking dinner for guests takes a lot of effort.*

questions.q: Why might a guest mention the flowers after a meal?
options: to say something kind without lying about the food
because they want to take the flowers home
because the flowers can be eaten
to change the subject to gardening
questions.why: Không thích món ăn vẫn có thể khen điều khác, thật lòng mà tế nhị.

questions.q: According to (D), you may leave the table as soon as you finish eating.
questions.why: Sai. *Wait to be excused before you leave the table.*

questions.q: According to (E), what might happen if you have great table manners?
options: You might have to cook next time.
You will sit at a different table.

parts.title: Part 3 · Picture tasks
parts.instr: Quan sát tranh minh hoạ trong sách và trả lời.

questions.q: How does the boy feel about the food?
options: He wants to cook it himself.
questions.why: Bịt mũi, nhăn mặt → không thích.
questions.alt: A boy holds his nose and pulls a face at a plate of food while a woman serves something from a bowl

questions.q: What would be the most polite thing for the boy to say?
questions.alt: A boy holds his nose and pulls a face at a plate of food while a woman serves something from a bowl

questions.q: Which paragraph matches this picture best?
questions.why: Đoạn C: *The flowers on the table are so pretty!*
questions.alt: A smiling girl at a table points to a vase of flowers while the host stands beside her holding a plate

parts.title: Part 4 · Gapped text
parts.instr: Đọc đoạn văn ngắn và chọn câu phù hợp cho mỗi chỗ trống. Có 2 câu thừa.
parts.text: Last night I had dinner at my friend Lucy's house. [1] I had never tried it before, and it looked a bit strange. [2] After dinner, I waited until Lucy's mum said we could leave the table. [3]
options: Her dad served a spicy fish curry.
Then I ran out of the room before dessert.
Her dad had ordered the same pizza that I eat every week.
I took a small bite, and to my surprise, it was delicious!
Before I went home, I thanked them both for inviting me.

parts.title: Part 5 · Words in context
parts.instr: Đoán nghĩa của từ/cụm từ dựa vào ngữ cảnh.

questions.q: *…if you really don't fancy fish eggs* (A). If you don't **fancy** something, you…
*Wait to be excused* (D). To **be excused** is to…
*…your manners will be finger-licking good* (E). Why is this phrase funny here?
options: It is usually used about tasty food, not manners.
Manners are a kind of food.
questions.why: **Finger-licking good** thường nói về đồ ăn ngon; tác giả dùng đùa cho phép lịch sự.
